verses.text: Six days before the Passover festival, Jesus came to Bethany. Lazarus lived there, the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
A dinner was given there in honour of Jesus. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those eating at the table with him.

Then Mary took about half a litre of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She poured it on Jesus' feet and wiped his feet with her hair. The whole house was filled with the sweet smell of the perfume.
But Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, one of Jesus' followers, who was later going to betray him, objected.
"Why was this perfume not sold?" he asked. "It was worth a whole year's wages. The money could have been given to the poor."
He did not say this because he cared about the poor. He said it because he was a thief. He looked after the money bag, and he used to help himself to what was put in it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She has kept this perfume for the day of my burial.
You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me."
A large crowd of Jewish people found out that Jesus was there. They came, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
because on account of him many of the Jewish people were leaving them and believing in Jesus.
The next day the large crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem.
They took branches from palm trees and went out to meet him, shouting, "Hosanna! Praise God! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the King of Israel!"
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as the Scriptures say:
"Do not be afraid, people of Zion. Look, your King is coming, sitting on a donkey's colt."

At first his followers did not understand these things. But after Jesus had been raised to glory, they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that people had done these things to him.
The crowd that had been with Jesus when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept telling others what they had seen.
That is why so many people went out to meet him. They had heard that he had done this miraculous sign.
So the Pharisees said to one another, "You can see that we are getting nowhere. Look, the whole world is following him!"
There were some Greeks among the people who went up to worship at the festival.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, with a request. "Sir," they said, "we would like to see Jesus."
Philip went to tell Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip went together to tell Jesus.
Jesus replied, "The time has come for the Son of Man to be given glory.
I tell you for certain, unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays just one seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds.
Anyone who loves their life will lose it. But anyone who hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
Whoever serves me must follow me. Where I am, my servant will also be. My Father will honour the one who serves me.
Now my heart is troubled. What shall I say? 'Father, save me from this hour'? No, it was for this very reason that I came to this hour.
Father, bring glory to your name!" Then a voice came from heaven: "I have brought glory to it, and I will bring glory to it again."
The crowd standing there heard it and said it was thunder. Others said, "An angel spoke to him."
Jesus said, "This voice was for your benefit, not mine.
Now is the time for this world to be judged. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself."
He said this to show what kind of death he was going to die.
The crowd answered, "We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain for ever. So how can you say, 'The Son of Man must be lifted up'? Who is this 'Son of Man'?"

Then Jesus told them, "The light will be with you for only a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, before darkness overtakes you. Whoever walks in the dark does not know where they are going.
Believe in the light while you have the light, so that you may become children of light." When he had finished speaking, Jesus went away and hid from them.
Even though Jesus had done so many miraculous signs in front of them, they still did not believe in him.
This happened so that the words of the prophet Isaiah would come true: "Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the power of the Lord been shown?"
That is why they could not believe. As Isaiah also said:
"He has blinded their eyes and made their hearts hard, so that they cannot see with their eyes or understand with their hearts, and turn to me, so that I could heal them."
Isaiah said this because he saw Jesus' glory, and he spoke about him.
Yet even among the leaders, many believed in him. But because of the Pharisees they would not say so openly, for fear that they would be thrown out of the synagogue.
They loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Then Jesus called out, "Whoever believes in me does not believe in me only, but also in the one who sent me.
Whoever looks at me is seeing the one who sent me.
I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in me should stay in darkness.
If anyone hears my words but does not obey them, I do not judge that person. I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
There is a judge for anyone who rejects me and does not accept my words. The very message I have spoken will judge them on the last day.
I have not spoken on my own. The Father who sent me commanded me what to say and how to say it.
I know that his command leads to eternal life. So whatever I say is just what the Father has told me to say."
